purpose: Build an editable Slalom-branded PowerPoint executive readout from approved shared content and a reviewed storyboard, without inventing findings or scraping a microsite DOM.

deliverable.name: Editable executive-readout PowerPoint deck from approved content
deliverable.path_or_form: A native .pptx with a fixture-derived manifest and HTML conversion preview
deliverable.note: The committed fixture is a labelled synthetic reconstruction. It demonstrates content-to-deck traceability but is not a customer deliverable.

human_baseline.note: No timed manual run or dated delivery-lead estimate exists for this exact deck.

golden_reference.note: Gada's approved deck has not yet been cleared for repository evaluation use. The synthetic fixture cannot serve as a human golden document.

expected_skill_invocations_note: Not observable in this deterministic runner. An agentic arm must extract these from the host session log.
required_clarifying_questions: Confirm the approved source content artifact.
Confirm the deck title, classification, accent, and slide sequence.
required_clarifying_questions_note: Not observable in this deterministic runner because it has no user turn.

inputs: Reviewed storyboard JSON for dense sections
environment: Fresh temporary output directory per run
Installed local dom-to-pptx and Chromium dependency

success_conditions: Declared source titles and selected source statements survive as native editable PPTX text.
Every source section is represented by the declared storyboard slide sequence.
The deck has native text and shapes, approved font and palette, classification, source notes, and resolved packaged images.
Deliberately corrupted PPTX packages are rejected with specific validation errors.
trajectory_requirements: Read the shared content contract rather than scraping the microsite DOM.
Do not invent findings, sources, or numbers.
known_failure_modes: Source content missing from native PPTX text
Storyboard does not cover a source section
Unapproved font, palette, dimension, logo, or source-note state
failure_mode_provenance_note: We guessed these failures from the skill contract and its existing negative validator cases; no agent trace error analysis has been performed.
